chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:
Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said:

“Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled that false accusation is of three kinds,” meaning three forms: “when he accuses a man of zina, when he says that his mother is an adulteress, and when he ascribes him to other than his father; in that there is a hadd of eighty.”

key_terms.الزِّنَى: illicit sexual intercourse, the accusation of which triggers the legal ruling here
key_terms.ثَمَانُونَ: eighty, the number of lashes in this ruling
key_terms.زَانِيَةٌ: an adulteress or fornicatress; used here in slander against one's mother
key_terms.لِغَيْرِ أَبِيهِ: to other than his father, meaning false attribution of lineage

ai.seo_question: What kinds of false accusation incur the hadd punishment of eighty lashes in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning three forms of slander that incur the hadd punishment. It identifies accusing someone of zina, slandering his mother with zina, or falsely attributing him to other than his father as offenses punishable by eighty lashes.
